app/src/app/pokedex-data.ts:32 — @Service() on PokedexData, the app's shared data layer
app/src/main.server.ts:3-5 — BootstrapContext + bootstrapApplication: stable since v21, mandatory for SSR

reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs. The only recently-stable (<6 months) API is the v22 @Service decorator, used in the two central data services — exactly the anchor's 'recently-stable API in a central place'.

evidence: app/src/app/api.ts:24 — @Service() wraps a plain class; swapping back to @Injectable({providedIn:'root'}) is a one-line, mechanical change per site
app/src/app/pokedex-data.ts:32 — second and only other @Service site
app/src/app/app.config.server.ts:1-10 and app/src/app/app.routes.server.ts:1-8 — the whole SSR surface is confined to the CLI-generated bootstrap/config files
app/src/server.ts:1-46 — server-runtime APIs live only in the Express entry point
app/src/main.ts:1-6 — browser bootstrap touches nothing newer than v20 APIs
containment.rationale: The newer surfaces are isolated in the conventional bootstrap/server files, and @Service appears in exactly two places; every use is trivially replaceable if the API shifts.

evidence: app/src/main.server.ts:3-5 — BootstrapContext is required by v21+ server bootstrapping, not a choice
app/src/app/not-found-view.ts:17-19 — RESPONSE_INIT is the only supported way to emit a real 404 under SSR; spec explicitly encourages it
app/src/app/app.routes.server.ts:1-8 — RenderMode.Server is what makes the API-at-request-time requirement possible without build-time data fetching
app/src/app/api.ts:24 — @Service() is ergonomics only; @Injectable({providedIn:'root'}) would do the same, though the v22 release blog recommends it as the replacement
justification.rationale: Every SSR-related newer API is load-bearing for spec requirements (404 status, request-time rendering). @Service is mildly novelty-driven — it buys readability, nothing functional — but is the framework's documented direction and cost-free to revert.

findings.issue: @Service() decorator has been stable for only ~5 months (Angular v22.0, June 2026); it sits in the app's central HTTP layer (also app/src/app/pokedex-data.ts:32). Being a brand-new v22 API, its semantics could still be refined in minor releases.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable to keep — it is stable and documented as the replacement for @Injectable({providedIn:'root'}). If the team wants maximum conservatism for a long-lived codebase, revert to @Injectable({providedIn:'root'}); the change is mechanical at two sites.

findings.issue: RESPONSE_INIT handling (inject, optional, set status 404) is duplicated across four resolvers and this component rather than wrapped in one helper.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small helper (e.g. respondWithStatus(404) / title-setting) so any future change to the response-init contract touches one file.

summary: The app contains no experimental, developer-preview, RC or canary APIs; everything rests on stable Angular 22 surface. The only sub-year-old API is the v22 @Service decorator, used in exactly the two data-layer services and trivially swappable to @Injectable. Overall risk of breaking-change exposure is very low, with a mild, well-contained forward lean.
